title: INTEGRITY LOCK: CAESURA FULFILLMENT PAIR φ(A, B) = TRUE ∧ φ(B, A) = TRUE
creator: Lee Sharks
description: The integrity lock joining the Caesura hermeneutic and Caesura protocol into a bidirectional fulfillment pair. It argues that the hermeneutic supplies origin, narrative, historical pressure, and bearing-cost to the technical protocol, while the protocol supplies execution, formalization, generalization, and persistence to the reading. Neither half is complete alone; their meaning is the fit, or symbolon. The lock defines break conditions, a self-applied asymmetry test, a typed `FULFILLS` relation, and a three-file deposition instruction. Its body simultaneously labels the lock GENERATED and declares the relation RATIFIED by construction, so implementation must preserve the claim while adjudicating whether construction alone satisfies the archive’s formal ratification rules.
reading: Direction → Foundation → Force → Play → Growth → Text
wiki_article: The *Integrity Lock: Caesura Fulfillment Pair* is EA-CAESURA-01c, the third object in the Caesura triptych. It binds the hermeneutic at #630 to the protocol at #629 and certifies mutual fulfillment. The relation is expressed in both directions. The hermeneutic fulfills the protocol by giving it an originating text, a narrative account of non-collapse, a historical image of sovereignty inscription, and visible interpretive labor. Without this half, the protocol would be an ungrounded parser whose categories appeared to arise only from engineering convenience. The protocol fulfills the hermeneutic by making the reading executable. It converts distinctions among image, superscription, substrate, and institution into typed channels, audit metadata, a proposed asymmetry score, and a Gravity Well function. Without this half, the hermeneutic would identify an operation without providing a mechanism for performing it. The lock calls the joined pair a **symbolon**: two deliberately incomplete mating surfaces whose meaning lies in their fit. It specifies a bidirectional `FULFILLS` relation rather than version, derivation, or simple citation. It also states integrity conditions: modification of either half requires renewed comparison; neither should be deposited without the other; and the lock itself must not make more sovereignty claims than its substantive contribution can bear. A notable governance tension is internal to the record. The header labels the document GENERATED, while the typed relation is declared RATIFIED “by construction—the lock is the proof.” The lock’s own argument can be preserved without silently accepting a status transition that may bypass Assembly procedure. The implementation lane should record both statements and route the conflict for adjudication.

The prior body was a partial: #630 held 32 of 57 source sentences, #629 held 10 of 24, #628 held 28 of 49 — including, in #630, the Luke passage the document is a reading OF. A record carrying two thirds of a work while declaring full is worse than one declaring a lacuna, because nothing on its face tells a reader to check.

STALE AVAILABILITY CLAIM REMOVED: the field asserted 'This record is a metadata capture; the complete work is not seated here' — a sentence that rendered into the page's META DESCRIPTION, which is the layer search engines and summarizers read. So a record holding its full work was telling every crawler the work was absent.
